speaker: Doctor
text: GREETING: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a skin condition on your left dorsal hand; please describe what it looks like and when you first noticed it. To help me narrow this down, have you experienced any fever, fatigue, or recent insect bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Diabetic Dermopathy (Shin spots on the hand)

Given your history of well-controlled diabetes and the location on your dorsal hand, I suspect diabetic dermopathy, which often presents as light brown, round or oval patches. Do you notice these lesions are slightly depressed, scaly, or have a "sock-like" appearance?
